tasks.title: Fix mergeBack exclusion to preserve tasks.json updates
tasks.description: Remove the `:!openspec/changes/` pathspec exclusion from the `git add` command in `worktree-manager.ts:187`. Change `['add', '--', ':!openspec/changes/', ':!.opencode/']` to `['add', '--', ':!.opencode/']`. This ensures tasks.json updates committed by ralph survive the mergeBack merge.
acceptanceCriteria: Line 187 in worktree-manager.ts no longer has `:!openspec/changes/` in the git add pathspec
The `:!.opencode/` exclusion is preserved
Typecheck passes
Existing tests pass
tasks.notes: Highest priority — 100% reproduction rate bug. The primary fix as decided in D1.

tasks.title: Commit tasks.json after ralph updates task status
tasks.description: After `writeTasksFile` in `ralph-executor.ts:472-473`, add a `git add` + `git commit` for tasks.json in the worktree. The commit message should reference the task ID and status. This is a belt-and-suspenders fix alongside T-001's mergeBack exclusion removal.
acceptanceCriteria: After writeTasksFile call, ralph-executor runs git add and git commit for tasks.json in the worktree
Commit message includes the task ID (e.g. 'chore(tasks): update T-001 passes=true')
The commit uses --no-verify flag
Typecheck passes
Existing tests pass
tasks.notes: Belt-and-suspenders with T-001. Can be implemented independently since both fixes address the same root cause from different angles.

tasks.title: Inject specs and tasks.json into buildReviewerPrompt
tasks.description: Add a `loadSpecContext(changeDir: string): string` helper to `artifact-prompt.ts` that reads all `*.md` files under `{changeDir}/specs/` recursively and reads `{changeDir}/tasks.json`, returning formatted `## Specs` and `## Tasks & Acceptance Criteria` sections. Insert the result into `buildReviewerPrompt`'s parts array between 'Change Directory' and 'Goal'. If specs/ doesn't exist, omit gracefully.
acceptanceCriteria: New `loadSpecContext` helper function exists in artifact-prompt.ts
Helper reads all *.md files under {changeDir}/specs/ recursively using glob
Helper reads {changeDir}/tasks.json
Output includes '## Specs' section with full spec content when specs/ exists
Output includes '## Tasks & Acceptance Criteria' section with tasks.json content
When specs/ directory doesn't exist, the specs section is omitted (no error thrown)
buildReviewerPrompt includes the spec context between Change Directory and Goal sections
Typecheck passes
Existing tests pass
tasks.notes: Design decision D2: read from changeDir path, no parameter changes needed.

tasks.title: Add Spec Compliance dimension to review.md
tasks.description: Add a new `### Spec Compliance` section to `review.md` between Security and Review Process, with instructions to check each AC from tasks.json against the implementation, verify exact values, and report per-criterion pass/fail. Update the Output Format template to include Spec Compliance alongside the existing four dimensions.
acceptanceCriteria: review.md has a '### Spec Compliance' section between Security and Review Process
Section instructs to check each acceptance criterion from tasks.json
Section instructs to verify exact values (colors, strings, formats, constants)
Section instructs to report per-criterion pass/fail with specific deviations
Output Format template includes '### Spec Compliance: PASS / FAIL' with [findings]
Typecheck passes

tasks.title: Enhance review-self-check.md to validate spec compliance coverage
tasks.description: Add a new 'Spec Compliance Coverage' section to `review-self-check.md` that checks: report has a '### Spec Compliance' section, each AC from tasks.json is explicitly addressed, findings are specific (not generic). If coverage is missing, the self-check rewrites the report.

Checks that report has a '### Spec Compliance' section
Checks that each AC from tasks.json is addressed in the report
Checks that findings reference specific spec requirements, not generic statements
Format section lists Spec Compliance alongside the existing four dimensions
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Depends on T-004 because the self-check validates a report that should have the Spec Compliance dimension.

tasks.title: Extract web utility functions for testability
tasks.description: Extract `formatTime` and `statusBadge` from `IssueDetailPage.tsx` into `src/lib/format-time.ts` and `src/lib/status-badge.ts`. Extract `formatTimeAgo` from `ExploreSessionList.tsx` into `src/lib/format-time.ts`. Extract `LEVEL_COLORS` and `LEVEL_CHIP_COLORS` from `LogsPage.tsx` into `src/lib/log-levels.ts`. Update all components to import from the new modules. Keep function signatures identical.
acceptanceCriteria: New file src/lib/format-time.ts exports formatTime and formatTimeAgo functions with identical behavior
New file src/lib/status-badge.ts exports statusBadge function with identical behavior
New file src/lib/log-levels.ts exports LEVEL_COLORS and LEVEL_CHIP_COLORS constants
IssueDetailPage.tsx, ExploreSessionList.tsx, and LogsPage.tsx import from the new modules
Web app builds successfully (npm run build in packages/cli/web)
Typecheck passes
tasks.notes: Design decision D5: extract for testing, don't move. Standard pattern for making component-internal functions testable.

tasks.title: Write unit tests for web utility functions

Test `statusBadge` for all IssueStatus values with exact Tailwind class assertions. Test `LEVEL_COLORS` and `LEVEL_CHIP_COLORS` for exact values. Tests should catch the specific regressions from Issue #30 (wrong color values, missing format cases).

Test file for formatTimeAgo exists covering sub-minute, minutes, hours, days, and 30+ day thresholds
Test file for statusBadge exists asserting exact Tailwind classes per IssueStatus value
Test file for LEVEL_COLORS and LEVEL_CHIP_COLORS exists asserting exact values for all log levels
Tests cover all IssueStatus enum values (Active, Paused, Blocked, Interrupted, default)
Changing any statusBadge color value or LEVEL_COLORS entry causes a test failure
Tests run successfully via vitest (npx vitest run in packages/cli/web)
